title: Starting a machine on Windows fails when there is a gvproxy/win-sshproxy orphan
body:
### Issue Description

The command `podman machine stop` shuts down the VM process and kills gvproxy or win-sshproxy. But if the VM is killed using another client (e.g. `wsl --shutdown`), gvproxy and win-sshproxy aren't killed. This becomes problematic when the machine is restarted and the 

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue with Hyperv:
1. `podman machine init --provider=hyperv --now`
2. `Stop-VM -Name "podman-machine-default"`
3. `podman machine start`

Steps to reproduce the issue with WSL:
1. `podman machine init --now`
2. `wsl --shutdown`
3. `podman machine start`




### Describe the results you received

On HyperV:
```
Starting machine "podman-machine-default"
time="2026-08-12T16:31:56+02:00" level=warning msg="detected port conflict on machine ssh port [35380], reassigning"
Error: could not start api proxy since expected pipe is not available: podman-machine-default
```

On WSL:
```
API forwarding for Docker API clients is not available due to the following startup failures.
        could not start api proxy since expected pipe is not available: podman-machine-default
```

Manually killing the gvproxy/win-sshproxy process and stopping/starting the machine solves the problem

### Describe the results you expected

At very least, we should handle the case of a gvproxy/win-sshproxy orphan at machine start. Either by reusing it or killing the existing instance and running a new one. Ideally, we should register a hook to kill gvproxy/win-sshproxy when the VM is killed (if the provider supports a shutdown hook).
